spec_provided_observability.name: Presence Pulse
spec_provided_observability.purpose: After every Reset, master can verify at least one slave is present on the bus (DQ goes LOW 15-60 µs after master release).

spec_provided_observability.name: CRC-8 over 64-bit ROM ID
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Last 8 bits of every ROM ID is a CRC-8 over the 56-bit (family code + serial) prefix; master can verify ROM-ID integrity end-to-end.

spec_provided_observability.name: CRC-8 over function-command payload
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Many function commands (e.g. DS18B20 Read Scratchpad) end with a CRC-8 over the data bytes; master can verify data integrity.

spec_provided_observability.name: Search ROM enumeration
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Master can enumerate all slaves on the bus by binary-tree Search ROM; missing slaves are detectable as enumeration mismatches over time.

spec_provided_observability.name: Bus-stuck-LOW detection
spec_provided_observability.purpose: If DQ does not return HIGH after master release, master can infer wiring fault or held-down slave.

notes: AN148 does NOT specify protocol-level error reporting or BIST. Reliability mechanisms are confined to (a) the CRC-8 over the 64-bit ROM ID and certain function-command payloads, and (b) the Presence Pulse as a coarse 'is anyone home' check. AN148 highlights search-algorithm robustness — Devices that physically present may appear and disappear in search results due to noise, parasite-power starvation, or signal reflections; reliable networks must implement debounce windows and tolerate transient enumeration failures. Master-end interface design (slew-rate control, dynamic pull-up, sample-time accuracy) is the primary lever for improving observability and reliability.
